result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection located beneath an elevated rail structure. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks, marked crosswalks, and signals are present, the environment is characterized by wide lanes and faded pavement markings.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are worn and faded, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a mid-block refuge, increasing exposure time.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and structural pillars near the intersection can block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection near the curb and overhead structure.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint crosswalks with high-visibility 'continental' markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide zebra-marked crosswalk and sidewalks under an elevated transit structure. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and a small median island are present, the overhead structure and large support pillars create significant shadows and potential sightline obstructions for both drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Large concrete support pillars for the elevated structure can block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left foreground, pillars supporting the blue structure

hazards.name: Low Ambient Light
hazards.description: The overhead structure creates deep shadows, reducing the visibility of pedestrians even during daylight hours.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire crossing area under the blue structure

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install additional high-intensity lighting under the structure specifically aimed at the crosswalk and sidewalk waiting areas.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position beyond the line of the support pillars.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add user-actuated flashing lights to the crossing signs to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians in the shadowed area.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals at a busy commercial hub beneath an elevated transit station. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the massive overhead structure and its support pillars create significant visual obstructions and deep shadows that may compromise pedestrian visibility.

hazards.name: Elevated structure pillars
hazards.description: Large support pillars for the elevated train tracks can block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians at the corners.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the intersection

hazards.name: Shadowing and low contrast
hazards.description: The overhead transit structure creates heavy shadows on the roadway, potentially making pedestrians less visible to motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway directly under the elevated tracks

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position beyond the support pillars.

interventions.title: Under-deck Lighting
interventions.description: Add high-intensity lighting to the underside of the elevated structure to improve visibility in shadowed areas.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is situated beneath an elevated transit structure, which provides shade but creates significant visual obstructions with its massive support pillars. While marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks are present, the pillars and overhead shadows reduce the visibility of pedestrians to motorists at the intersection.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large steel support pillars for the elevated track block the view between drivers and pedestrians at the crossing points.
hazards.location_in_image: Support pillars at the corners of the intersection

hazards.name: Low Visibility due to Shadows
hazards.description: The overhead structure creates deep shadows that can make pedestrians less visible to drivers, especially during transition periods of the day.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to move the pedestrian waiting area past the line of the support pillars, improving sightlines for both drivers and walkers.

interventions.title: Enhanced Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian-scale lighting under the elevated structure to illuminate the crosswalk area and sidewalk.
